rv.q: Laurence Connor and James Powell's rendition of Boublil and Schonberg's musical reinvention of Victor Hugo's novel is an absolute blinder.
Yes, the original, 35 year-old version has vanished, but make no mistake: Les Mis is back to stay.
But it’s clear from this major retread that it still has bags of mileage – as does this gorgeously reborn Edwardian theatre.
He has shrewdly opened it not with one of Sondheim’s plinkety-plonk tooth-grinders, but with a revival of Boublil and Schönberg’s box-office cert Les Misérables.
I worried less about the adaptation and was impressed by the hurtling speed of the staging and the shadowy beauty of the design.
I don’t think anybody could realistically see this imperfect, absurd, magnificent show and suggest that its crown as London’s longest-runner is in any danger.
Les Misérables is one of the best musicals of all time and this new version will undoubtedly run for years.
It gets everything right and delivers an unforgettable evening of musical theatre.
Not quite a rebirth then, but in its way still magnifique.
With tickets for as little as £20 it's a piece of West End magic that really shouldn't be missed.

cn.t: The revamped production thrives in its refurbished home, with critics praising its leaner staging and timeless emotional power. The updated version showcases the iconic score more strongly, proving the show's enduring appeal after 35 years.
